claim: The pedagogical argument: 'Patch an LFO into the leak time constant: you hear the membrane becoming leakier in real time, the ramp curving and straightening, the timbre sweeping from warm to bright' — per-sample math lets the student hear the equation directly, where a control-rate parameter puts a boundary in the patch.

pieces.what: Start with one leaky integrate-and-fire ramp at a fixed leak; then patch an LFO into leak tau and switch between signal-rate and block-rate (128-sample steps) modulation — hear the ramp curve and straighten, and hear the zipper the control-rate version adds as the LFO speeds up.
The zero guard: sweep leak tau toward 0 with and without max() — the unguarded version goes NaN and silent; the guarded one hits a floor.
The modular argument: route an audio-rate oscillator into the same leak input and hear modulation become timbre — any output into any input.
